Chokepoint Watch: Robotics

As of 2026-10-19
Edition 1
Previous edition: first edition

ChangedFirst edition. No earlier edition was found, so this run opens the board with two chokepoints and one rejection.

Toprob-1: Tb/Dy-bearing NdFeB magnets and heavy rare earths under China's April 2025 export licensing (MOFCOM No. 18), which is still in force.

NextTesla Q3 results on 2026-10-21, then the 2026-11-10 expiry of MOFCOM's suspension (No. 70) of the October 2025 rare-earth controls.

Evidence, not a trade: this page has no buy or sell views, no sizing, and no share prices.

P primary L lead map analyst's map, not evidence contradicted unexamined

Predictions settled this week

None. This is the first edition, so no predictions have come due.

The board

rob-1 · deep-dive

Tb/Dy-bearing NdFeB magnets and heavy rare earths under China's export licensing

New

Layer: heavy rare-earth (Dy, Tb) metal, alloy and oxide, and NdFeB magnet material that contains Tb or Dy, as named in MOFCOM/GACC Announcement 2025 No. 18. These are high-coercivity magnet grades used in servo and frameless torque motors.

Chain

  1. Factory automation demand drives industrial robot orders. JARA reports Apr–Jun 2026 orders of ¥312.7bn, +40.0% y/y. P
  2. Each robot joint uses a servo or frameless torque motor. map
  3. Compact high-temperature motors use sintered NdFeB with Dy/Tb added for coercivity. map
  4. China requires a licence to export Tb/Dy-bearing NdFeB magnet material and Dy/Tb metal, alloy, oxide and compounds (No. 18). P
  5. Outside China, Dy/Tb separation is small. Lynas is the disclosed producer, but it gives no annual capacity. P (no tonnage)

Six steps

Constraint primary

The constraint is an export licence for each shipment of the No. 18 items (unit: licensed shipments, in tonnes). The control instrument is primary. Its effect on how many tonnes are released is not measured here.

"经国务院批准，决定对下列物项实施出口管制：" … "本公告自发布之日起正式实施。"MOFCOM & GACC, Announcement 2025 No. 18, 2025-04-04 · mofcom.gov.cn · item list covers Sm, Gd, Tb, Dy, Lu, Sc and Y as metal/alloy, oxide and compound, including NdFeB magnet material containing Tb or Dy
No. 18 is not among the announcements suspended in Nov 2025. No. 70 suspends only Nos. 55–58 and 61–62: "自即日起至2026年11月10日"MOFCOM & GACC, Announcement 2025 No. 70, 2025-11-07 · mofcom.gov.cn
Demand vs supply lead

Robot demand is ordered, not hoped for: JARA orders were +40% y/y P, IFR reports 2025 installations of 600,000+ P, and Yaskawa robot orders were +33% L. The US government says shipments are below "appropriate levels", but it says this of "rare earths" in general. Under the layer rule, that supports no magnet-layer step. Lynas reports strong demand for Dy/Tb, which shows demand is strong, not that it exceeds qualified capacity.

"…with the goal of ensuring shipment levels return to appropriate levels." "The next exchange will occur by November 2026."The White House, fact sheet on the China state visit, 2026-09-25 · whitehouse.gov
"This will assist Lynas to meet the strong demand for Dy and Tb from outside China customers."Lynas Rare Earths, Quarterly Report, quarter to 30 Jun 2026, 2026-07-22 · ASX
Relief primary (magnet layer only)

New magnet capacity outside China is real at the magnet layer: eVAC has about 2,000 t/yr and USA Rare Earth is going from 600 to 1,200 mtpa; Neo Narva's about 2,000 t/yr is L only. None of these documents names its Dy/Tb feed, and no Dy/Tb separation capacity is disclosed in tonnes per year. Customer qualification of motor-grade magnets typically takes 12–24 months map, and that is the binding term.

"The facility has a nameplate capacity of about 2,000 metric tons per year, with room to scale in the coming years."Vacuumschmelze, press release 04/2026 "Opening Ceremony Sumter", 2026-07-16 · vacuumschmelze.com
"Phase 1a is expected to ramp to a run rate capacity of 600 mtpa by the end of Q4 2026." "USAR anticipates total active production capacity at Stillwater of 1,200 mtpa in Q1 2027."USA Rare Earth, Stillwater Phase 1a commissioning release, 2026-03-26 · usare.gcs-web.com
"Magnet qualification at Independence advanced through additional deliveries for customer qualification" … "while construction of our 10X facility accelerated."MP Materials, Q2 2026 results (8-K Ex. 99), 2026-08-06 · sec.gov · no magnet tonnage given
Control unexamined

The holder of the constraint is the Chinese state, which issues the licences. China's share of Dy/Tb separation and of sintered NdFeB output is very high map, but no primary share figure was opened this run.

Capture lead

The state captures leverage, not margin. Producers outside China see higher prices: Lynas's average selling price hit a record A$98.2/kg P. That figure covers all products, so it is not Dy/Tb-specific and does not show who books magnet-layer economics.

"The average selling price across all rare earth products increased to a record A$98.2/kg in the June quarter."Lynas, Quarterly Report, 2026-07-22 · ASX
Invalidation primary

The Nov 2025 deal suspended the wider October 2025 package. The US also states that China would issue general licences. Those licences would ease No. 18 flows if they were issued, but no MOFCOM general-licence text was found.

"China will issue general licenses valid for exports of rare earths, gallium, germanium, antimony, and graphite…" "The general license means the de facto removal of controls China imposed since 2023."The White House, fact sheet on the US–China deal, 2025-11-01 · whitehouse.gov · US characterisation, "rare earths" layer only

Verdicts

Scarcity: plausible, lead-gradeThe control is primary and in force. The tonnage shortfall at the magnet layer is unproven.
Capture: state-heldThe leverage sits with MOFCOM licensing. Producers outside China gain on price, but the evidence is not layer-specific.
Investability: unresolvedThe holder is a state. Listed producers outside China (Lynas, MP, USAR) exist, but their dilution and balance sheets were not checked.

Bear checks

  • Dilution: unexamined for MP, USAR or Lynas this run.
  • GAAP margins: unexamined.
  • Customer concentration: MP lists its Apple agreement and the DoW price-protection agreement in its risk factors P. The share of revenue was not checked.
  • Cash vs debt: unexamined.
  • Second source: yes at the magnet layer (eVAC, USAR) P. Thin at the Dy/Tb layer, where no tonnage is disclosed.
  • Bypass architecture: no robot-specific release on reduced- or zero-rare-earth motors was found. Searched; none.
  • Pull-forward / humanoid volumes: this chokepoint does not rely on humanoids. Industrial orders are up, but some may be restocking ahead of 2026-11-10 map.
  • Policy reversal: this is the main risk. An extension of No. 70 plus general licences for No. 18 items would ease it sharply. The next US–China exchange is due "by November 2026" P.
  • Layer error: the US fact sheets speak of "rare earths" and support no magnet step. The magnet-layer claim rests on No. 18 alone.

Kill criteria

  • By 2026-11-30, MOFCOM issues general licences that cover No. 18 items (Tb/Dy-bearing NdFeB material, Dy/Tb metal and oxide) for US, EU or Japan end users. This would mean downgrade, or kill if paired with the next item.
  • GACC data show NdFeB magnet exports (HS 8505.11) at or above their 2024 monthly average for three consecutive months.
  • A robot or servo maker states in a filing or on a call that magnet supply has normalised, or qualifies Dy/Tb-free grades in servo motors.

Predictions

rob-p1By 2026-11-30, MOFCOM will have published an announcement that extends or replaces the suspension in Announcement 2025 No. 70 beyond 2026-11-10, so the October 2025 measures (Nos. 55–58 and 61–62) do not take effect as written. Settled by a MOFCOM/GACC announcement.
rob-p2By 2027-03-31, USA Rare Earth will report total active NdFeB magnet production capacity at Stillwater of at least 1,200 mtpa. Settled by its own Q4 2026 results release or Form 10-K.

Status since last edition: new.

rob-2 · deep-dive (watch)

Planetary roller screws for humanoid linear actuators

New · not qualified

Layer: actuator component (inverted and standard planetary roller screws), plus the internal thread-grinding capacity that makes them. It stays on the board as a watch item, because humanoid demand is not yet ordered at volume.

Chain

  1. Humanoid programmes: Tesla says first-generation Optimus lines "are being installed in anticipation of production in 2026". L
  2. Linear actuators are about 30% of the humanoid BOM in Schaeffler's view and use planetary roller screws. P
  3. Roller screws need precision internal thread grinding. map
  4. Chinese screw suppliers are at the sample stage. L

Six steps

Constraint lead

The unit would be qualified roller-screw sets per year. Trade press says domestic screws have passed "0 to 1" but face three hurdles to "1 to 10" (Jiemian, about 2026-09-01) L.

Demand vs supply contradicted

Demand is mostly prototype or aspirational. Schaeffler reports prototype orders, not series volume. Wuxi Best's humanoid roller-screw revenue is samples only (RMB 223k, 0.03% of H1 revenue) L. UBTech delivered about 600 Walker S2 units in H1 L, which is ordered but small.

"28 prototype orders across 14 global Humanoid OEMs" · "Schaeffler aims to achieve a market share of >10 % by 2030 in the rapidly growing humanoid market"Schaeffler, "Powering Humanoid Motion" investor presentation, 2026-01-12 · schaeffler.com
Relief lead

Many entrants are tooling up. Wuzhou Xinchun reports a planned 980k sets/yr in Xinchang (trade press) L, and Qinchuan says it has P0-grade internal thread grinders L. If volume does arrive, qualification time, not machine count, is likely to bind map.

Control lead

Incumbents are GSA, Rollvis and Ewellix (Schaeffler) map. Reports that Optimus Gen 2 uses GSA screws are trade press L.

Capture unexamined

Nothing to capture until series orders exist.

Invalidation primary

Unitree in-sources its core components, which shifts the actuator decision to the robot maker.

"公司坚持高性能通用机器人及核心部组件全栈自研" (full-stack in-house R&D of robots and core components)Unitree, STAR Market draft prospectus (上会稿), 2026-05-25 · cninfo

Verdicts

Scarcity: not shownSupply is at samples, but so is demand.
Capture: not shownThere are no series contracts.
Investability: n/aExposure is a tiny revenue share at listed suppliers.

Bear checks

  • Dilution, GAAP margins, cash vs debt: unexamined.
  • Customer concentration: likely high. Tesla is the reference customer map.
  • Second source: many Chinese entrants are sampling L. That argues against a lasting chokepoint.
  • Bypass architecture: no primary evidence of a switch to ball screws was found. In-sourcing (Unitree) is primary.
  • Humanoid volumes that don't arrive: this is the main risk. Tesla's Q3 2026 production release has no Optimus figure P.
  • Policy reversal: not applicable, except through magnets in the actuator motor (see rob-1).
  • Layer error: "screw" revenue at suppliers often mixes ball and roller screws. Only roller-specific disclosures are used here.

Kill criteria

  • By 2027-04-19, no humanoid OEM has disclosed in a filing, release or call a series production rate of at least 10,000 units/yr or a roller-screw supply contract at series volume. Then kill this as aspirational.
  • Two or more non-incumbent suppliers announce batch qualification at a humanoid OEM. A second source would then exist.
  • A leading humanoid OEM discloses a switch to ball screws or another bypass in its linear actuators.

Predictions

rob-p3By 2027-02-15, neither Tesla's Q3 2026 nor its Q4 2026 update or earnings call will state cumulative Optimus production above 1,000 units. Settled by Tesla's quarterly update and call.

Cross-theme hooks

  • Tb/Dy-bearing NdFeB also feeds defence actuators and guidance, EV traction motors and wind generators. eVAC names automotive traction and a DLA agreement P.
  • Precision reducers and servo motion are shared with semiconductor equipment. HDS cites chip-equipment demand alongside robots P.
  • Precision roller screws and thread grinding are shared with aerospace and defence electromechanical actuation and with machine tools map.

Next questions

  • Does MOFCOM extend, replace or let lapse the No. 70 suspension, and does it issue general licences for No. 18 items? Look at the MOFCOM announcements index and the export-control portal around 2026-11-07 to 11-10.
  • What do NdFeB magnet exports (HS 8505.11) look like for September and October 2026? Look at GACC data on stats.customs.gov.cn, released around the 20th of each month.
  • Does Tesla give an Optimus volume or name actuator suppliers? Look at the Q3 2026 update and call on 2026-10-21.
  • What are MP Materials' 10X timing, magnet tonnage and heavy rare-earth separation figures, and what is Lynas's Dy/Tb tonnage? Look at MP's Q3 2026 results (early Nov) and Lynas's September 2026 quarterly report on the ASX.
  • Does HDS show backlog and book-to-bill tightening? Look at its Q2 FY3/2027 tanshin on TDnet (early Nov), and also check six-axis F/T sensors, which were not examined this week.

Run notes

  • Step 0: the artifact list was searched (all 64 artifacts). No "Chokepoint Watch: Robotics" exists, so this is edition 1.
  • Pages were opened by research subagents through a fetch tool that returns verbatim fragments, sometimes cut at about 125 characters. Quotes are copied as returned, and long quotes may be fragments of the source sentence.
  • MOFCOM's export-control portal (exportcontrol.mofcom.gov.cn) was blocked by robots.txt or the proxy. No MOFCOM general-licence document was found, and no 2026 MOFCOM announcement on No. 70 was found.
  • Not reached: GACC 2026 magnet export data; BIS, Federal Register and DoD/DOE 2026 magnet awards; MP's Q2 call transcript; Lynas's FY2026 annual report; HDS's backlog table; the Nabtesco, Leaderdrive, Yaskawa and UBTech primary filings; Tesla's own Q2 2026 update PDF; NSK, THK, Timken, SKF and Shanghai Beite.
  • Unverified: Lynas's Dy/Tb output of 19 t in the quarter (trade press); Neo Narva's 2,000 t/yr (trade press); Leaderdrive's subsidiary figures; JARA's production growth figure.
  • Not examined: six-axis F/T and tactile sensors, dexterous hands, robot compute, batteries, encoders, heat treatment and test equipment.
  • Tool calls: about 84 (four research subagents used 76, the main run about 8). This is slightly over the 80 budget.
